title: Probing $τ$ lepton dipole moments at future Lepton Colliders
summary: The electric and magnetic dipole moments of the electron and of the muon provide stringent tests of the Standard Model and sensitive probes of new physics. By contrast, the corresponding dipole moments of the $τ$ lepton remain weakly constrained. This study explores the potential of future lepton colliders, focusing on the $e^+e^-$ Future Circular Collider and a multi-TeV muon collider, to probe $τ$ dipole moments. We consider multiple channels, including $\ell^+\ell^- \to τ^+τ^-$ ($\ell=e,μ$), associated Higgs production $μ^+μ^- \to τ^+τ^- H$, radiative Higgs decays $H \to τ^+τ^-γ$, and vector-boson scattering $\ell^+\ell^- \to \ell^+\ell^-τ^+τ^-$ and $μ^+μ^- \to \barνντ^+τ^-$. Our results show that these facilities are highly complementary and can extend existing bounds by several orders of magnitude.

AI.tldr: Future lepton colliders (FCC-ee and multi-TeV muon collider) can dramatically improve constraints on tau lepton electric and magnetic dipole moments by several orders of magnitude through multiple production channels.
AI.motivation: While electron and muon dipole moments are well-constrained and serve as sensitive probes of new physics, tau lepton dipole moments remain weakly constrained despite their potential to test the Standard Model and reveal new physics.
AI.method: Study explores multiple production channels at future lepton colliders: tau pair production (ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻), associated Higgs production (μ⁺μ⁻ → τ⁺τ⁻H), radiative Higgs decays (H → τ⁺τ⁻γ), and vector-boson scattering processes (ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ → ℓ⁺ℓ⁻τ⁺τ⁻ and μ⁺μ⁻ → ν̄ντ⁺τ⁻).
AI.result: Future lepton colliders (FCC-ee and multi-TeV muon collider) are highly complementary and can extend existing bounds on tau dipole moments by several orders of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: Future lepton colliders offer powerful capabilities to probe tau lepton dipole moments through multiple complementary channels, potentially revealing new physics beyond the Standard Model.

title: Probing Neutrino Compositeness with Invisible and Displaced Signals
summary: We explore the possibility that neutrinos couple to an interacting sterile sector, providing a novel portal that generalizes the heavy neutral lepton portal to a composite setting. For a low confinement scale, high-energy neutrino beams can disintegrate into collimated sprays of hidden states, referred to as dark jets. This dynamics gives rise to two characteristic signatures in high energy neutrino beams. First, long-lived dark resonances can enhance the neutral-current to charged-current ratio. Second, shorter-lived dark states produced in neutrino neutral currents can produce single or multiple displaced vertices and even emerging jets, depending on the kinematics. These signals probe regions of parameter space beyond existing constraints from meson, electroweak, and Higgs decays, as well as from searches for displaced decays at beam dump experiments. We study these phenomena within broad classes of ultraviolet completions and identify scenarios in which high-energy neutrino beams provide leading sensitivity to neutrino compositeness. Such scenarios generically induce higher-dimensional contact interactions, which we classify and study alongside their complementary experimental signatures. Finally, we outline an experimental program spanning both the intensity and energy frontiers. Near-term neutrino facilities (DUNE, FPF) and running flavor experiments (LHCb, Belle II) can probe neutrino compositeness through neutrino disintegration into dark jets and displaced B-meson decays. Future colliders, particularly the Future Circular Collider (FCC-ee), will ultimately provide the strongest sensitivity to the compositeness scale via displaced Z decays.

AI.tldr: Neutrinos may couple to an interacting sterile sector, creating a composite portal that leads to neutrino disintegration into dark jets, with signatures including enhanced NC/CC ratios and displaced vertices at neutrino facilities and colliders.
AI.motivation: The paper explores neutrino compositeness through coupling to an interacting sterile sector, generalizing the heavy neutral lepton portal to a composite setting to probe new physics beyond existing constraints from meson, electroweak, and Higgs decays.
AI.method: The authors study neutrino disintegration into collimated sprays of hidden states (dark jets) at low confinement scales, analyze characteristic signatures including enhanced neutral-current to charged-current ratios and displaced vertices, and examine scenarios within broad classes of ultraviolet completions that induce higher-dimensional contact interactions.
AI.result: High-energy neutrino beams can probe neutrino compositeness through dark jet production, with signatures accessible at near-term facilities (DUNE, FPF) and flavor experiments (LHCb, Belle II). Future colliders like FCC-ee will provide strongest sensitivity to compositeness scale via displaced Z decays, probing parameter space beyond existing constraints.
AI.conclusion: Neutrino compositeness through coupling to an interacting sterile sector provides novel signatures in high-energy neutrino beams, with an experimental program spanning intensity and energy frontiers offering leading sensitivity to neutrino compositeness beyond current constraints.

title: A Busy Higgs Signal
summary: Higgs final states are prime targets in the search for physics beyond the Standard Model. In the conventional picture, $SU(2)$ symmetry together with the Goldstone Equivalence Theorem correlates Higgs and gauge-boson final states, implying comparable sensitivity in channels such as $hh$, $ZZ$, and $WW$ in searches for heavy resonances. In this work, we identify a mechanism to parametrically violate this expectation. We show that higher-order Higgs couplings can induce an electroweak-symmetry-breaking enhancement that selectively amplifies Higgs-rich final states, allowing them to become the leading discovery channels of new resonances. For scalar resonances, this can make di-Higgs the dominant bosonic signal. For resonance masses higher than a couple of TeV, it also opens resonant tri-Higgs and four-Higgs channels as well-motivated search targets. The same underlying mechanism extends to heavy fermionic and vector resonances, where it can similarly enhance channels such as $ht$, $Zh$, and $γh$. We present this framework in effective field theory, demonstrate possible UV completions, and discuss its implications for collider searches.

AI.tldr: Higher-order Higgs couplings can parametrically violate the Goldstone Equivalence Theorem expectation, selectively enhancing Higgs-rich final states to become leading discovery channels for new resonances.
AI.motivation: The conventional picture based on SU(2) symmetry and Goldstone Equivalence Theorem predicts comparable sensitivity in Higgs and gauge-boson final states (hh, ZZ, WW) for heavy resonance searches. However, this work identifies a mechanism to parametrically violate this expectation, potentially making Higgs-rich channels more sensitive discovery avenues.
AI.method: The authors use effective field theory framework to demonstrate how higher-order Higgs couplings can induce electroweak-symmetry-breaking enhancement. They show this mechanism selectively amplifies Higgs-rich final states and present possible UV completions to validate the framework.
AI.result: For scalar resonances, di-Higgs (hh) can become the dominant bosonic signal. For resonance masses above ~2 TeV, resonant tri-Higgs and four-Higgs channels emerge as well-motivated search targets. The mechanism extends to heavy fermionic and vector resonances, enhancing channels like ht, Zh, and γh.
AI.conclusion: Higher-order Higgs couplings provide a mechanism to parametrically violate the Goldstone Equivalence Theorem expectation, making Higgs-rich final states potentially leading discovery channels for new resonances across scalar, fermionic, and vector sectors, with implications for collider search strategies.

title: Magic and Non-Clifford Gates in Topological Quantum Field Theory
summary: Non-Clifford gates, used to generate quantum magic, are essential for universal quantum computation. We show that non-Clifford gates arise naturally from path integrals in topological quantum field theories, where their magic-generating properties are determined by the algebraic data of the theory. In Chern-Simons theory, we construct the Ising interaction gate, whose generator is prepared by path integration over simple three-boundary manifolds, and show that it produces non-local magic away from discrete Clifford points. We show that the Toffoli gate is obstructed in $SU(2)_1$ by the $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fusion structure, while $SU(2)_3$ is the minimal theory supporting the required conditional logic, given the density of the mapping class group in the projective unitary group on the manifold boundary. Finally, we demonstrate that the T gate arises as a path integral in Dijkgraaf-Witten theory, with gauge group $\mathbb{Z}_4$, where a single Dehn twist on the boundary torus produces the gate without approximation. These results show that topological path integrals construct gates in multiple levels of the Clifford hierarchy, and across distinct classes of field theories, with implications for topological quantum computing.

AI.tldr: Topological quantum field theory path integrals naturally generate non-Clifford gates essential for universal quantum computation, with different theories producing gates at various levels of the Clifford hierarchy.
AI.motivation: Non-Clifford gates are crucial for universal quantum computation as they generate quantum magic, but their natural origins in topological quantum field theories remain to be systematically explored.
AI.method: Using path integrals in topological quantum field theories (Chern-Simons and Dijkgraaf-Witten theories) to construct quantum gates, analyzing algebraic data, fusion structures, and mapping class group properties to determine gate realizability.
AI.result: Constructed Ising interaction gate from Chern-Simons theory producing non-local magic; showed Toffoli gate obstructed in SU(2)_1 but realizable in SU(2)_3; demonstrated T gate arises from Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with Z_4 gauge group via Dehn twist.
AI.conclusion: Topological path integrals systematically construct gates across multiple levels of the Clifford hierarchy in different field theories, providing a natural framework for gate generation with implications for topological quantum computing architectures.

title: Cornering MeV-GeV Axions and Dark Photons with LDMX
summary: Axion-like particles (ALPs), the QCD axion, and dark photons in the MeV-GeV mass range are motivated by various dark matter models and the strong CP problem, and are ubiquitous in extensions of the Standard Model. A long-standing blind spot for experimental searches is the sub-100 MeV mass range, where the particle lifetime is too long to be constrained by prompt-decay collider searches yet too short to be reached by beam-dump experiments. We investigate and estimate the sensitivity of the Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX) to such axions and dark photons, motivated by the clean environment in which these particles can be produced and by the near-target tracking capabilities of LDMX. With reasonable charged track and momentum reconstruction capabilities, we find that LDMX could close much of this low-mass blind spot for axions and dark photons.

AI.tldr: LDMX can probe sub-100 MeV axions and dark photons, closing a sensitivity gap between prompt-decay collider searches and beam-dump experiments.
AI.motivation: Axion-like particles, QCD axions, and dark photons in MeV-GeV range are motivated by dark matter models and strong CP problem, but sub-100 MeV mass range remains a blind spot due to intermediate lifetimes that evade both prompt-decay collider searches and beam-dump experiments.
AI.method: Investigate sensitivity of Light Dark Matter eXperiment (LDMX) to such particles, leveraging its clean production environment and near-target tracking capabilities with reasonable charged track and momentum reconstruction.
AI.result: LDMX could close much of the low-mass blind spot for axions and dark photons in the sub-100 MeV mass range.
AI.conclusion: LDMX provides a promising experimental approach to probe the previously inaccessible sub-100 MeV mass window for axions and dark photons, addressing a long-standing sensitivity gap in particle physics searches.

title: Generalized Complexity Distances and Non-Invertible Symmetries
summary: Non-invertible symmetries of a quantum field theory (QFT) are a natural generalization of unitary symmetries, but in which the product of operators does not satisfy a group multiplication law. We show that such symmetry operations on states define a collection of quantum gates for a parallel quantum computation scheme that includes post-selection / projection as a gate. Structures such as gate complexity and more geometric complexity measures generalize to this setting. We provide a class of distance / distinguishability measures that extend the standard notion of distance for Lie groups to both continuous and discrete non-invertible symmetries, as well as more general linear combinations of unitary quantum gates. We illustrate these considerations by computing the distance between non-invertible symmetries in some 4D and 2D QFTs. We find that the simple objects of a symmetry category can be highly complex computationally.

AI.tldr: Non-invertible symmetries in QFT define quantum gates for parallel computation with post-selection, with new complexity measures and distance metrics extending beyond group theory.
AI.motivation: To extend quantum computation and complexity theory to non-invertible symmetries, which generalize unitary symmetries but lack group structure, and to develop distance measures for these operations.
AI.method: Treat non-invertible symmetry operations as quantum gates in parallel computation schemes with post-selection/projection, develop complexity measures and distance/distinguishability metrics that extend Lie group distances to continuous/discrete non-invertible symmetries and linear combinations of unitary gates.
AI.result: Established framework for analyzing non-invertible symmetries as computational resources, computed distances between non-invertible symmetries in 4D and 2D QFTs, found that simple objects in symmetry categories can be computationally complex.
AI.conclusion: Non-invertible symmetries provide a rich framework for quantum computation beyond unitary gates, with new complexity measures and distance metrics that reveal computational complexity even in simple symmetry category objects.

title: Logarithmic EW corrections at two-loop
summary: We present the implementation of next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) electroweak (EW) virtual corrections at next-to-leading logarithmic (NLL) accuracy in the amplitude generator OpenLoops. The implementation covers the automated computation of processes involving massless fermions and transversely polarised vector bosons. For energies above the EW scale, logarithmic EW corrections are strongly enhanced in the tails of kinematic distributions of key LHC processes, reaching several tens of percent at NLO and several percent at NNLO. The two-loop implementation is validated against analytical results from the literature. We present phenomenological results for representative LHC processes and discuss the role of two-loop EW corrections in reducing theoretical uncertainties from missing higher-order contributions.

AI.tldr: Implementation of NNLO electroweak virtual corrections at NLL accuracy in OpenLoops for massless fermion processes with transverse vector bosons, validated against analytical results and applied to LHC phenomenology.
AI.motivation: Logarithmic electroweak corrections are strongly enhanced at high energies in LHC processes, reaching tens of percent at NLO and several percent at NNLO, necessitating precise calculations for accurate theoretical predictions.
AI.method: Automated computation of NNLO electroweak virtual corrections at NLL accuracy implemented in the OpenLoops amplitude generator, covering processes with massless fermions and transversely polarized vector bosons.
AI.result: Two-loop implementation validated against analytical literature results; phenomenological results for representative LHC processes demonstrate significant EW corrections and reduction of theoretical uncertainties from missing higher-order contributions.
AI.conclusion: The implementation enables precise calculation of NNLO EW corrections for LHC processes, reducing theoretical uncertainties and improving the accuracy of predictions for high-energy tails where EW corrections are strongly enhanced.

title: Beyond the Dilute Instanton Gas: Resurgence with Exact Saddles in the Double Well
summary: The path-integral approach to the double well has long been limited by the dilute instanton gas approximation. We show that if the finite Euclidean-time structure is taken seriously by using exact saddles, the dilute gas can be sidestepped, allowing the partition function and energy levels to be computed systematically. At each instanton order, the full resurgent structure -- which saddles contribute, what asymptotic growth is expected and how ambiguities cancel -- is encoded in a finite-dimensional Picard--Lefschetz contour integral over the quasi-zero modes with a clear geometric interpretation. Working at finite $T$ is essential: the dilute instanton gas can only access the ground-state splitting, whereas the exact finite-$T$ computation systematically produces the non-perturbative energy splittings for all excited states, including their full dependence on the level number. The key ingredients -- Weierstrass elliptic functions for the saddles, Lamé operators for the fluctuations and Picard--Fuchs equations for the periods -- form a coherent mathematical framework that both overlaps and complements that of Exact WKB.

AI.tldr: Exact finite-T computation of double-well potential using exact saddles instead of dilute instanton gas approximation, enabling systematic calculation of partition function and energy levels with full resurgent structure.
AI.motivation: Overcome limitations of dilute instanton gas approximation in path-integral approach to double well by using exact saddles and finite Euclidean-time structure to compute partition function and energy levels systematically.
AI.method: Use exact saddles (Weierstrass elliptic functions), compute fluctuations via Lamé operators, handle periods via Picard-Fuchs equations, and encode resurgent structure in finite-dimensional Picard-Lefschetz contour integrals over quasi-zero modes.
AI.result: Systematic computation of non-perturbative energy splittings for all excited states with full dependence on level number, going beyond ground-state splitting accessible via dilute instanton gas.
AI.conclusion: Finite-T computation with exact saddles provides coherent mathematical framework (overlapping/complementing Exact WKB) that sidesteps dilute gas approximation and reveals complete resurgent structure of double-well system.

title: Astrophysical bounds on the high-energy evolution of neutrino mixing
summary: While conventional oscillation experiments measure neutrino mixing parameters with high precision, these measurements are strictly confined to sub-TeV scales. At higher energies, renormalization-group effects can cause these parameters to evolve with the transferred momentum, $Q$. High-energy and ultra-high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, spanning TeV to EeV energies, probe high values of $Q$ unreachable by conventional experiments, offering an unprecedented test of high-energy mixing. We use the flavor composition of these neutrinos -- the relative proportions of $ν_e$, $ν_μ$, and $ν_τ$ -- to constrain this evolution, both phenomenologically and within dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory. We account for astrophysical uncertainties -- an unavoidable requirement to obtain realistic results, even though this weakens the bounds. Although present IceCube measurements lack the sensitivity to detect this running, we forecast that upcoming multi-detector combinations will place unprecedented bounds on the high-energy evolution of neutrino mixing.

AI.tldr: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos (TeV-EeV) probe momentum-dependent neutrino mixing evolution via flavor composition analysis, with current IceCube data insufficient but future multi-detector setups promising constraints.
AI.motivation: Conventional oscillation experiments measure neutrino mixing parameters only at sub-TeV scales, but renormalization-group effects cause these parameters to evolve with momentum transfer Q at higher energies. High-energy astrophysical neutrinos provide a unique probe of this high-energy mixing evolution.
AI.method: Use flavor composition (relative proportions of ν_e, ν_μ, ν_τ) of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos to constrain momentum-dependent mixing evolution. Analyze both phenomenologically and within dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory framework, while accounting for astrophysical uncertainties.
AI.result: Current IceCube measurements lack sensitivity to detect momentum-dependent mixing evolution. However, forecasts show that upcoming multi-detector combinations will place unprecedented bounds on the high-energy evolution of neutrino mixing parameters.
AI.conclusion: High-energy astrophysical neutrinos offer a unique window into momentum-dependent neutrino mixing evolution at scales unreachable by conventional experiments. While current data is insufficient, future multi-detector measurements will provide powerful constraints on high-energy mixing parameter evolution.

title: Quantum correction to the diffusion term in stochastic inflation from composite-operator matching in Soft de Sitter Effective Theory
summary: In the framework of Soft de Sitter Effective Theory (SdSET), the Fokker-Planck equation for the late-time dynamics of the massless minimally coupled scalar field and its extension to the Kramers-Moyal equation are obtained from operator mixing of composite operators of the effective superhorizon field. We construct the formalism for composite-operator renormalisation, mixing and matching in dimensional regularisation, allowing for computations beyond the leading order. The general formalism is illustrated in free SdSET, which already features non-trivial structures including the well-known diffusion coefficient for stochastic inflation. As explicit examples in the interacting theory, we renormalise the one-loop bispectrum and the two-loop one-point function of the composite operator $\varphi_+^2$, and match them onto their full-theory counterparts. These results allow us to determine the next-to-leading order (two-loop) correction to the diffusion term of the Fokker-Planck equation of stochastic inflation for the first time.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a composite-operator renormalization formalism in Soft de Sitter Effective Theory (SdSET) to compute higher-order corrections to stochastic inflation, specifically obtaining the two-loop correction to the Fokker-Planck equation's diffusion term.
AI.motivation: To systematically compute higher-order corrections in stochastic inflation beyond leading order, particularly for the Fokker-Planck equation, by developing a rigorous framework for composite-operator renormalization, mixing, and matching in the SdSET formalism.
AI.method: Constructs composite-operator renormalization formalism in SdSET using dimensional regularization, analyzes operator mixing of composite operators of the effective superhorizon field, and demonstrates the approach through explicit calculations in free and interacting theories.
AI.result: Successfully renormalizes one-loop bispectrum and two-loop one-point function of composite operator φ₊², matches them to full-theory counterparts, and determines the next-to-leading order (two-loop) correction to the diffusion term of the Fokker-Planck equation for stochastic inflation.
AI.conclusion: The developed formalism enables systematic computation of higher-order corrections in stochastic inflation, with the two-loop diffusion term correction representing a significant advancement beyond previous leading-order results.

title: Wave-envelope dark matter beyond the monochromatic paradigm
summary: Ultralight dark matter searches widely assume that signals are monochromatic, with a single frequency set by the mass. This assumption is generally violated in the presence of field mixing, even when the constituent fields have similar frequencies. Instead, dark matter signals can exhibit a two-timescale structure with intrinsic slow modulation. We demonstrate that mixing between ultralight wave dark matter fields induces a parametric structure, leading to a scenario we refer to as wave-envelope dark matter, in which a slow-beating envelope emerges alongside the primary oscillation. This results in distinctive features such as slow modulation and characteristic sideband structures in the frequency spectrum, beyond the conventional monochromatic expectation. As a representative example, we briefly discuss implications for neutrino observables.

AI.tldr: Dark matter signals from mixed ultralight fields exhibit two-timescale structure with slow modulation and sidebands, not monochromatic signals.
AI.motivation: Conventional ultralight dark matter searches assume monochromatic signals, but this assumption breaks down when multiple fields mix, requiring new analysis approaches.
AI.method: Analyze field mixing between ultralight wave dark matter fields, showing it creates parametric structure with slow-beating envelopes and characteristic sideband features.
AI.result: Mixed fields produce wave-envelope dark matter with distinctive two-timescale structure: primary oscillation plus slow modulation and sideband spectral features.
AI.conclusion: Dark matter signals from mixed ultralight fields are not monochromatic; they exhibit complex temporal and spectral structure requiring new search strategies, with implications for neutrino observables.

title: Exact Toda Black Holes of Rank-2 Lie Groups
summary: We consider Einstein gravity coupled to two Maxwell fields and one dilatonic scalar, and construct spherically-symmetric and static black holes that are charged under both Maxwell fields in general $D$ dimensions. We find that for suitable dilaton couplings, the equations of motion can be cast into one-dimensional Toda equations of all rank-2 Lie groups. We devise a brute-force approach to obtain the most general but remarkably elegant solutions to the Toda equations. This allows us to construct exact black holes associated with all the rank-2 Lie groups. The $B_2$ and $G_2$ Toda black holes are new. We study their thermodynamics and verify explicitly an earlier claim in the literature that all these thermodynamic quantities can be derived without having to solve for these black hole solutions.

AI.tldr: Exact black hole solutions in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity with two Maxwell fields in D dimensions, solved via Toda equations of rank-2 Lie groups, with new B₂ and G₂ Toda black holes and thermodynamic analysis.
AI.motivation: To construct exact spherically-symmetric static black hole solutions charged under two Maxwell fields in Einstein-dilaton gravity, leveraging Toda equation formalism to obtain general solutions for all rank-2 Lie groups.
AI.method: Consider Einstein gravity coupled to two Maxwell fields and one dilatonic scalar in D dimensions; for suitable dilaton couplings, reduce equations of motion to one-dimensional Toda equations of rank-2 Lie groups; devise brute-force approach to obtain general elegant solutions to Toda equations.
AI.result: Construct exact black hole solutions associated with all rank-2 Lie groups (A₂, B₂, C₂, G₂); B₂ and G₂ Toda black holes are new; study thermodynamics and verify earlier claim that thermodynamic quantities can be derived without solving full black hole solutions.
AI.conclusion: Successfully obtained general exact black hole solutions for all rank-2 Toda systems in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity, confirming thermodynamic consistency and demonstrating power of Toda equation approach for constructing charged black hole solutions.

title: Search for the $Λ_cΣ_c$ and $\barΛ_cΣ_c$ dibaryon structures via the QCD sum rules
summary: In this paper, we construct eight pairs of hexaquark currents to search the $Λ_cΣ_c$ and $\barΛ_cΣ_c$ dibaryon states via QCD sum rules. We show that the two currents of each pair are equivalent and we choose one of them to calculate the masses and pole residues of ground states. For either $Λ_cΣ_c$ or $\barΛ_cΣ_c$, the $J^P$ of the considered hexaquark currents are $0^-$, $0^+$, $1^+$ and $1^-$, respectively. We found three possible molecular states, they are $Λ_cΣ_c$ dibaryon with the $J^P=1^+$ and $\barΛ_cΣ_c$ dibaryons with the $J^P=0^-$ and $1^-$. The other five are unlikely to form the bound dibaryon states, and we assign them as the resonance states.

AI.tldr: QCD sum rule analysis of ΛcΣc and Λ̄cΣc dibaryon states using hexaquark currents reveals three possible molecular states and five resonance states.
AI.motivation: To investigate the existence and properties of ΛcΣc and Λ̄cΣc dibaryon states using QCD sum rules, specifically searching for possible molecular and resonance states formed from charm baryons.
AI.method: Constructed eight pairs of hexaquark currents (four for ΛcΣc and four for Λ̄cΣc) with various quantum numbers (0⁻, 0⁺, 1⁺, 1⁻). Used QCD sum rules to calculate masses and pole residues of ground states, identifying molecular vs resonance states based on binding properties.
AI.result: Found three possible molecular states: ΛcΣc dibaryon with Jᴾ=1⁺, and Λ̄cΣc dibaryons with Jᴾ=0⁻ and 1⁻. The other five configurations are unlikely to form bound dibaryon states and are assigned as resonance states.
AI.conclusion: QCD sum rule analysis suggests the existence of specific ΛcΣc and Λ̄cΣc molecular dibaryon states with particular quantum numbers, while other configurations likely exist as resonances rather than bound states.

title: Carroll fermions, expansions and the lightcone
summary: We investigate fermions on Carrollian manifolds. We complement previous intrinsic analysis by deriving Carrollian fermion actions from a relativistic Dirac theory via a systematic expansion in the speed of light ($c$). We then study relativistic fermions in light-cone coordinates and their connection to Carrollian fermions in one lower dimension. This follows from the recent observation that the Poincaré algebra, written in lightcone coordinates contains (two) co-dimension one Carroll sub-algebras. Our results establish a clear bridge between intrinsic Carrollian constructions, small $c$-expansion and light-cone dynamics. In the process, we understand why Carrollian fermions in $D$-dimensions have features that relate them to relativistic fermions in both $D$ and $(D+1)$ dimensions.

AI.tldr: Carrollian fermion actions derived from relativistic Dirac theory via systematic c-expansion, connecting to light-cone dynamics and revealing dimensional relationships.
AI.motivation: To bridge intrinsic Carrollian constructions with relativistic origins by deriving Carrollian fermion actions from Dirac theory and exploring connections through light-cone coordinates.
AI.method: Systematic expansion of relativistic Dirac theory in speed of light (c), analysis in light-cone coordinates, and identification of Carroll sub-algebras within Poincaré algebra.
AI.result: Established clear connection between intrinsic Carrollian constructions, small-c expansion, and light-cone dynamics; explained why Carrollian fermions in D-dimensions relate to relativistic fermions in both D and (D+1) dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a comprehensive bridge between different approaches to Carrollian fermions, unifying intrinsic constructions, relativistic expansions, and light-cone dynamics while explaining dimensional relationships.

title: Inflaton Regeneration via Scalar Couplings: Generic Models and the Higgs Portal
summary: The standard cosmological paradigm assumes that the inflaton field becomes dynamically negligible during the post-reheating evolution of the Universe. We demonstrate that this assumption fails for a broad class of inflationary models where the potential behaves as a monomial form $V(φ) \propto φ^k$ (with $k \ge 4$) around the minimum. In such scenarios, the effective inflaton mass depends on the field amplitude and vanishes asymptotically as the Universe expands. This vanishing-mass mechanism renders the inflaton kinematically accessible to the thermal plasma long after reheating, facilitating the regeneration of inflaton quanta through 1-to-2 decays and 2-to-2 scatterings of bath particles. This mechanism is quite generic and the coupling responsible for reheating can be constrained if the inflaton is overproduced, while the inflaton quanta can constitute dark matter in specific scenarios. Furthermore, if reheating occurs via the Standard Model Higgs portal, the process can be further constrained by big bang nucleosynthesis, cosmic microwave background, and colliders such as the LHC. This mechanism provides a new framework for probing post-inflationary reheating.

AI.tldr: The inflaton can remain dynamically significant after reheating in monomial potentials (k≥4) due to vanishing effective mass, enabling thermal regeneration and potential dark matter production.
AI.motivation: Challenge the standard cosmological assumption that the inflaton becomes dynamically negligible after reheating, showing this fails for monomial inflationary potentials where the inflaton's effective mass vanishes asymptotically.
AI.method: Analyze inflationary models with monomial potentials V(φ)∝φ^k (k≥4) around the minimum, demonstrating that the vanishing effective mass allows the inflaton to remain kinematically accessible to the thermal plasma, enabling regeneration through 1-to-2 decays and 2-to-2 scatterings of bath particles.
AI.result: The inflaton can be overproduced, constraining reheating couplings; inflaton quanta can constitute dark matter in specific scenarios; Higgs portal reheating can be constrained by BBN, CMB, and LHC data.
AI.conclusion: The vanishing-mass mechanism provides a new framework for probing post-inflationary reheating, challenging standard assumptions about inflaton dynamics after inflation.

title: Mechanical properties of proton in the momentum space
summary: We study the parametrization of the energy-momentum tensor for the case of a proton in momentum space in terms of gravitational transverse momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs). These gravitational TMDs are investigated with the inclusion of higher-twist contributions to predict the mechanical properties, specifically the transverse pressure and shear force distributions, along with the polarization-dependent $Π^q_S$ and $Π^q_A$ terms. The corresponding distributions are computed individually for both $u$ and $d$ quark flavors. The calculations have been performed in the light-cone framework using the spectator diquark model. A strong binding contribution to the transverse pressure is observed in the low-momentum space for both quark flavors of the proton.

AI.tldr: Study of gravitational TMDs for proton in momentum space using spectator diquark model, predicting mechanical properties like transverse pressure and shear force distributions for u and d quarks.
AI.motivation: To investigate the parametrization of proton's energy-momentum tensor in momentum space using gravitational transverse momentum-dependent distributions (TMDs), including higher-twist contributions to predict mechanical properties.
AI.method: Light-cone framework with spectator diquark model, computing gravitational TMDs including higher-twist contributions for both u and d quark flavors individually.
AI.result: Strong binding contribution to transverse pressure observed in low-momentum space for both u and d quark flavors of the proton; computed polarization-dependent Π^q_S and Π^q_A terms along with shear force distributions.
AI.conclusion: Gravitational TMDs provide valuable framework for studying proton's mechanical properties in momentum space, revealing significant binding effects in low-momentum region for both quark flavors.

title: One-Loop Quantum Corrections to the Casimir Effect for Rough Plates in the Low-Temperature Regime
summary: We present a theoretical analysis of the one-loop effective potential of a self-interacting real scalar field in the presence of two parallel conducting plates with geometric roughness. Using WKB methods to evaluate the spectral density of the modified Laplace-Beltrami operator, together with contour integration within a $ζ$-function regularization scheme, we derive analytical expressions for the quantum corrections to the effective potential induced by perturbative boundary roughness and finite temperature. Furthermore, we compute explicit contributions to the Casimir energy and to the topological mass generation associated with the geometry.

AI.tldr: Theoretical analysis of quantum field effects near rough conducting plates using WKB and ζ-function regularization to compute effective potential, Casimir energy, and topological mass generation.
AI.motivation: To understand how geometric roughness on conducting plates affects quantum field phenomena, including the one-loop effective potential, Casimir energy, and topological mass generation in scalar field theory.
AI.method: Uses WKB methods to evaluate spectral density of modified Laplace-Beltrami operator, combined with contour integration within a ζ-function regularization scheme to derive analytical expressions for quantum corrections.
AI.result: Derived analytical expressions for quantum corrections to effective potential induced by perturbative boundary roughness and finite temperature, with explicit contributions to Casimir energy and topological mass generation.
AI.conclusion: Geometric roughness on conducting plates significantly modifies quantum field effects, providing analytical tools to compute corrections to effective potential, Casimir energy, and topological mass in realistic boundary conditions.

title: Exploring non-equilibrium effects in sequential freeze-in
summary: Freeze-in of multi-component dark sectors is governed not only by the interaction with the thermal plasma, but also by their internal dynamics. Full thermalisation within the dark sector is not guaranteed, raising the question of impact of departures from local thermal equilibrium onto the evolution and ultimately relic abundance and momentum distribution of dark matter. In this work we explore this question in a minimal two-scalar model, which can give rise to observable signatures in indirect detection and long-lived particle searches at forward physics experiments. Focusing on the phenomenologically viable regions, we analyse the impact of non-thermal evolution on the dark matter abundance, finding deviations of up to an order of magnitude between the full phase-space treatment and the traditional number-density approach. Our results highlight the importance of phase-space level computation for accurate freeze-in predictions and further motivate dedicated numerical tools for studying the evolution of multi-component dark sectors at the phase space level.

AI.tldr: Freeze-in dark matter predictions can deviate by an order of magnitude when accounting for non-thermal evolution within multi-component dark sectors versus traditional number-density approaches.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses how internal dynamics within dark sectors can prevent full thermalization, potentially impacting dark matter relic abundance and momentum distribution predictions. Traditional freeze-in calculations assume local thermal equilibrium, but departures from equilibrium could significantly affect results.
AI.method: The authors use a minimal two-scalar model to explore non-thermal evolution in dark sectors. They employ a full phase-space treatment rather than traditional number-density approaches, analyzing phenomenologically viable regions where observable signatures could appear in indirect detection and long-lived particle searches.
AI.result: The analysis reveals deviations of up to an order of magnitude in dark matter abundance predictions between the full phase-space treatment and traditional number-density approach. This demonstrates significant impact of non-thermal evolution on freeze-in predictions.
AI.conclusion: Phase-space level computations are crucial for accurate freeze-in predictions in multi-component dark sectors. The results motivate development of dedicated numerical tools for studying dark sector evolution at the phase space level, particularly for models with observable signatures in indirect detection and forward physics experiments.

title: Emergent States and Algebras from the Double-Scaling limit of Pure States in SYK
summary:
Recent work has emphasized a subtlety of large- $N$ limits in AdS/CFT: a sequence of pure states in the microscopic theory need not remain pure with respect to the emergent algebra of observables. We study this phenomenon for Kourkoulou-Maldacena (KM) states in the double-scaling limit of the SYK model, and show that their ensemble-averaged algebraic description depends crucially on which observables survive the limit. For fermionic operators of size $N^{1/2}$, generic operators converge to the usual chord operators of double-scaled SYK. The resulting von Neumann algebra is the standard Type II$_1$ factor, and the KM pure states at infinite temperature converge to the tracial state, so generic probes lose access to microscopic purity. We then identify a class of operators adapted to the KM state that also survives the double-scaling limit. Since the KM state may be viewed as a projection inside the tracial state, these become dressed chord creation and annihilation operators. Once included, the limiting algebra becomes Type I$_\infty$ and the limiting state becomes pure. This gives a concrete example in which adding a sufficiently state-adapted operator to the emergent algebra restores access to the purity of the underlying state.
  We further show that correlators of the dressed operators admit exact modified chord-diagram rules, derive analytic expressions for uncrossed $2n$-point and crossed four-point functions, analyze their finite-temperature semiclassical and Schwarzian limits, study a deformation of the chord Hamiltonian that produces bound states and extends the correspondence with JT gravity plus an EOW brane to general brane tension, and identify an emergent $U(1)$ symmetry together with its finite-$N$ violation. Finally, we discuss analogies with boundary algebras proposed for black hole interiors and closed universes, and suggest lessons from our construction for both.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that in double-scaled SYK, whether KM states appear pure or mixed depends on which observables survive the limit - adding state-adapted operators restores access to microscopic purity.
AI.motivation: To understand how the emergent algebra of observables in AdS/CFT can obscure microscopic purity, and to provide a concrete example where state-adapted operators reveal underlying purity.
AI.method: Study Kourkoulou-Maldacena states in double-scaling limit of SYK model, analyze which operators survive the limit, identify state-adapted operators, derive modified chord-diagram rules, and analyze various limits and deformations.
AI.result: With generic operators, KM states converge to tracial state (Type II₁ algebra), hiding purity. With state-adapted operators, algebra becomes Type I∞ and state becomes pure. Derived exact chord rules, analytic expressions for correlators, and connections to JT gravity with EOW branes.
AI.conclusion: The emergent algebra's description of microscopic purity depends crucially on which observables survive the limit, providing lessons for boundary algebras in black hole interiors and closed universes.

title: Rescattering effects in near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction
summary: We investigate near-threshold $J/ψ$ photoproduction off the nucleon, focusing on hadronic rescattering effects induced by open-charm meson-baryon intermediate states. Beyond the conventional Pomeron-exchange mechanism, the $\bar D^0Λ_c^+$ and $\bar D^{*0} Λ_c^+$ channels are incorporated within an effective Lagrangian framework. The relevant production amplitudes are evaluated at tree level from $t$-, $s$-, and $u$-channel diagrams in a gauge-invariant manner. The resulting total and $t$-dependent differential cross sections are compared with recent near-threshold data from the GlueX, $J/ψ$-007, and CLAS experiments at Jefferson Lab. We find that the open-charm rescattering contributions significantly improve the description of the data, particularly at large momentum transfer, and naturally generate cusp-like structures near the $\bar D^0 Λ_c^+$ and $\bar D^{*0} Λ_c^+$ thresholds in the GlueX data. We further present predictions for the associated open-charm processes $γp \to \bar D^{(*)0} Λ_c^+$, whose cross sections are estimated to be of the order of 5 nb.

AI.tldr: Study of near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction on nucleons incorporating open-charm meson-baryon rescattering effects, showing improved data description and predicting associated open-charm processes.
AI.motivation: Investigate hadronic rescattering effects in near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction beyond conventional Pomeron-exchange mechanisms, addressing discrepancies in experimental data from GlueX, J/ψ-007, and CLAS experiments.
AI.method: Effective Lagrangian framework incorporating open-charm channels (D̄⁰Λc⁺ and D̄*⁰Λc⁺) with gauge-invariant tree-level evaluation of t-, s-, and u-channel diagrams.
AI.result: Open-charm rescattering significantly improves data description, especially at large momentum transfer, and generates cusp-like structures near open-charm thresholds; predicts associated open-charm processes with cross sections ~5 nb.
AI.conclusion: Hadronic rescattering through open-charm intermediate states is crucial for understanding near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction and provides testable predictions for open-charm production processes.

title: Half-BPS Impurity Backgrounds and Supersymmetry
comment: 8 pages. Accepted for publication in Eur. Phys. J. C
summary: We develop a rigid $\mathscr{N} =(1,1)$ superspace framework for spatially inhomogeneous impurity deformations in $D=1+1$ dimensions by embedding the impurity profile into a real background superfield (spurion). This spurionic completion provides a manifestly supersymmetric description at the level of the action and offers a systematic route to identify which inhomogeneous backgrounds preserve a nontrivial subset of supercharges. Focusing on static interface-type configurations, we determine the half-BPS condition on the spurion background and the corresponding supersymmetry projector. In the resulting half-BPS sector we derive the associated first-order BPS equation for static bosonic matter configurations and establish an exact Bogomol'nyi completion of the static energy, yielding a sharp bound saturated by BPS solutions. We further comment on how explicit coordinate dependence and derivative-dependent impurity couplings can obstruct the Bogomol'nyi structure, thereby motivating spurionic extensions that retain supersymmetric control over inhomogeneous deformations.

AI.tldr: Rigid N=(1,1) superspace framework for spatially inhomogeneous impurity deformations in 1+1D using spurion embedding, enabling systematic identification of supersymmetry-preserving backgrounds and derivation of half-BPS conditions, first-order equations, and Bogomol'nyi bounds.
AI.motivation: To develop a systematic framework for studying spatially inhomogeneous impurity deformations in supersymmetric theories while maintaining manifest supersymmetry at the action level, overcoming limitations of explicit coordinate dependence and derivative-dependent couplings that obstruct Bogomol'nyi structure.
AI.method: Embed impurity profile into a real background superfield (spurion) within rigid N=(1,1) superspace in 1+1 dimensions. Use spurionic completion for manifestly supersymmetric action description. Derive half-BPS conditions for static interface-type configurations, determine supersymmetry projector, and establish Bogomol'nyi completion of static energy.
AI.result: Systematic identification of supersymmetry-preserving inhomogeneous backgrounds, derivation of half-BPS condition and corresponding projector, first-order BPS equations for static bosonic matter configurations, and exact Bogomol'nyi completion yielding sharp energy bound saturated by BPS solutions.
AI.conclusion: Spurionic framework provides powerful approach to maintain supersymmetric control over inhomogeneous deformations, enabling systematic study of BPS structures in impurity-modified theories while avoiding obstructions from explicit coordinate dependence and derivative couplings.

title: Status of the hadronic light-by-light contribution to the muon $g-2$ and holographic QCD predictions
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Proceedings contribution for the Workshop FCCP2025, Anacapri, Italy, Sep 29 - Oct 1, 2025, to appear in EPJ Web of Conferences
summary: We review the recent progress made with regard to the hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) contribution to the Standard Model prediction of the muon anomalous magnetic moment and how well this compares with predictions from holographic QCD models, which had predicted larger contributions from axial vector mesons and short-distance constraints than the White Paper of 2020. A new holographic prediction concerns tensor-meson contributions, which in holographic QCD play a significant role in short-distance constraints beyond the Melnikov-Vainshtein constraint. When matching also the symmetric longitudinal short-distance constraint, the resulting prediction for the tensor-meson transition form factors agree well with available singly virtual data, but lead to different results than the traditional quark-model ansatz and a sizable positive contribution that could explain the remaining current tension between lattice and data-driven results for the HLbL contribution.

AI.tldr: Holographic QCD models predict larger axial vector meson contributions to HLbL than the 2020 White Paper, with tensor mesons playing a key role in short-distance constraints, potentially explaining tensions between lattice and data-driven HLbL results.
AI.motivation: To review progress on hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) contribution to muon g-2, comparing holographic QCD predictions with the 2020 White Paper, and address tensions between lattice and data-driven results.
AI.method: Review of recent HLbL progress using holographic QCD models, focusing on axial vector mesons and tensor mesons, with analysis of short-distance constraints including Melnikov-Vainshtein and symmetric longitudinal constraints.
AI.result: Holographic QCD predicts larger axial vector contributions than White Paper; tensor mesons significantly impact short-distance constraints beyond Melnikov-Vainshtein; tensor-meson transition form factors match singly virtual data but differ from quark-model predictions; yields sizable positive contribution that could resolve lattice vs data-driven HLbL tensions.
AI.conclusion: Holographic QCD models provide enhanced HLbL contributions from axial vector and tensor mesons that better satisfy short-distance constraints and may explain current discrepancies between lattice and data-driven approaches to muon g-2.

title: Thermality Breakdown in Null-Shifted Rindler Wedges
summary: We investigate the behaviour of quantum fields in null-shifted Rindler wedges and analyse the particle spectra perceived by accelerated observers associated with these null deformations. Unlike the standard Unruh effect, our analysis compares two accelerated frames connected by a null displacement. We consider both massive scalar and Dirac fields, constructing their corresponding mode solutions in Rindler coordinates. Using normalised field expansions, we compute the Bogoliubov transformations between modes defined in the two null-shifted wedges. Our results demonstrate a fundamental breakdown of thermality: the presence of mass modifies the mode structure, rendering the characteristic exponential mixing of frequencies absent. This suggests that the massive field remains unexcited on this background, leading to a manifestly nonthermal response. These findings highlight that thermality in accelerated frames depends sensitively on the conformal symmetry of the field, which is broken by the introduction of a mass term.

AI.tldr: Analysis of quantum fields in null-shifted Rindler wedges reveals nonthermal particle spectra for accelerated observers, with mass breaking conformal symmetry and preventing thermal excitation.
AI.motivation: To investigate how quantum fields behave in null-shifted Rindler wedges and analyze particle spectra perceived by accelerated observers in these null-deformed geometries, going beyond the standard Unruh effect by comparing two accelerated frames connected by null displacement.
AI.method: Construct mode solutions for both massive scalar and Dirac fields in Rindler coordinates, use normalized field expansions to compute Bogoliubov transformations between modes defined in two null-shifted wedges, and analyze the resulting particle spectra.
AI.result: Fundamental breakdown of thermality: mass modifies mode structure, eliminating characteristic exponential mixing of frequencies, suggesting massive fields remain unexcited on this background and yield manifestly nonthermal response.
AI.conclusion: Thermality in accelerated frames depends sensitively on conformal symmetry of the field, which is broken by mass terms, leading to nonthermal particle spectra in null-shifted Rindler wedges.

title: Phenomenology of Vanishing Effective Majorana Mass with a Sterile Neutrino under Cosmological and JUNO Constraints
summary: In the present work we investigate the phenomenological implications of a vanishing effective Majorana neutrino mass within a $3+1$ neutrino framework adding a eV-scale sterile neutrino beside three active neutrino states in light of latest cosmology driven bounds on sum of neutrino masses ($\sum_{i}m_i$). We explore the parameter space where the destructive interference between active and sterile states leads to vanishing amplitude, $M_{ee}$, of neutrinoless double beta ($0νββ$) decay. The allowed parameter space has been identified and predictions have been obtained taking into account the latest Planck and DESI+CMB bound on $\sum_{i}m_i$. We find that these bounds restrict the sterile mixing angle $θ_{14}$ and the lightest active neutrino mass. Furthermore, we incorporate the refined precision data from JUNO experiment regarding solar oscillation parameters ($θ_{12}, Δm_{21}^2$). We find that the sterile neutrino parameters like $θ_{14}$ may not be sensitive to the JUNO precision measurements as the constraint imposed by precise $θ_{12}$ is washed out by new cancellations driven through additional CP violating phases leading to vanishing $|M_{ee}|$.

AI.tldr: Study of vanishing effective Majorana neutrino mass in 3+1 neutrino framework with eV-scale sterile neutrino, exploring parameter space where destructive interference leads to vanishing neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude under cosmological bounds.
AI.motivation: Investigate phenomenological implications of vanishing effective Majorana neutrino mass in 3+1 neutrino framework, where destructive interference between active and sterile states could lead to zero neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude despite non-zero neutrino masses.
AI.method: Analyze parameter space in 3+1 neutrino model with eV-scale sterile neutrino, incorporating latest cosmological bounds on sum of neutrino masses from Planck and DESI+CMB, and refined solar oscillation parameters from JUNO experiment.
AI.result: Cosmological bounds restrict sterile mixing angle θ₁₄ and lightest active neutrino mass; JUNO precision measurements on θ₁₂ may not constrain θ₁₄ due to cancellations from additional CP violating phases that lead to vanishing |Mₑₑ|.
AI.conclusion: Vanishing neutrinoless double beta decay amplitude can occur in 3+1 framework through destructive interference, with cosmological bounds providing stronger constraints than oscillation parameter precision measurements due to CP phase cancellations.

title: Glauber-Lachs formula-based analysis of three-pion Bose-Einstein correlation data at 7 TeV from the LHCb Collaboration
summary: We combine the Glauber--Lachs formula from quantum optics and the two-component picture for pion production to analyze data on two- and three-pion Bose--Einstein correlation at 7 TeV from the LHCb Collaboration. For the pion exchange function $E_{\rm 2B}$, we chose a dipole form and an inverse one-and-a-half pole form. The extensions are computed in the configuration space of 4-dimensional Euclidean space ($ξ=\sqrt{|\bm r_1-\bm r_2|^2+(t_1-t_2)^2}$).

AI.tldr: Analysis of LHCb 7 TeV pion Bose-Einstein correlations using Glauber-Lachs formula and two-component picture with dipole and inverse one-and-a-half pole forms for pion exchange function in 4D Euclidean space.
AI.motivation: To analyze two- and three-pion Bose-Einstein correlation data from LHCb at 7 TeV using quantum optics formalism and pion production models to understand pion source characteristics and interactions.
AI.method: Combines Glauber-Lachs formula from quantum optics with two-component picture for pion production. Uses dipole form and inverse one-and-a-half pole form for pion exchange function E_2B. Computes extensions in 4D Euclidean configuration space (ξ = √|r₁-r₂|²+(t₁-t₂)²).
AI.result: Not specified in abstract, but method applied to analyze LHCb 7 TeV data on two- and three-pion Bose-Einstein correlations.
AI.conclusion: Not specified in abstract, but approach enables analysis of pion correlation data using quantum optics formalism and specific pion exchange models in Euclidean space.

title: Fermionic modes of D-instanton wormholes from broken local supersymmetry
summary: In low-energy supergravity treatment of type IIB superstring on general D-instanton wormhole profiles in the bulk, we obtain non-vanishing scalar two-point functions in addition to the vanishing $\langle τ^* τ^* \rangle$ that corresponds to the BPS amplitude detected by two D-instantons at their respective boundaries. This is exploited to show that the modes of broken local supersymmetry in the bulk deliver the fermionic (diagonal) modes on the boundaries through the deformation by the form of current-current two point functions propagating on the tree level cylinder geometry. Our treatment is generalizable to multi D-instanton cases and general Euclidean branes.

AI.tldr: Non-vanishing scalar two-point functions emerge in type IIB supergravity from D-instanton wormholes, revealing broken supersymmetry modes connecting bulk and boundary fermions via current-current correlations on cylinder geometry.
AI.motivation: To understand how D-instanton wormhole configurations in type IIB superstring theory generate non-trivial scalar correlations beyond the vanishing BPS amplitude, and to explore the connection between broken local supersymmetry modes in the bulk and boundary fermionic degrees of freedom.
AI.method: Low-energy supergravity treatment of type IIB superstring on general D-instanton wormhole profiles in the bulk, analyzing scalar two-point functions and their relation to current-current correlations propagating on tree-level cylinder geometry.
AI.result: Obtained non-vanishing scalar two-point functions in addition to the vanishing ⟨τ*τ*⟩ BPS amplitude, showing that broken local supersymmetry modes in the bulk deliver fermionic (diagonal) modes on boundaries through deformation by current-current two-point functions.
AI.conclusion: The approach successfully connects bulk supersymmetry breaking to boundary fermionic modes via wormhole-mediated correlations, with generalizability to multi D-instanton cases and general Euclidean branes.

title: Production of doubly heavy quarkonium associated with two heavy quarks via top quark decays
summary: In this paper, we analyze the $1 \rightarrow 4$ decay channel for the production of doubly heavy quarkonium, $(b\bar{c})$ or $(c\bar{c})$, via top-quark decays, $t \to (b\bar{c}) + c + c + \bar{s}$ and $t \to (c\bar{c}) + b + c + \bar{s}$, within the framework of nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD). The dominant contributions are considered in color-singlet S-wave states, i.e., $(b\bar{c})[^1S_0]$, $(b\bar{c})[^3S_1]$, $(c\bar{c})[^1S_0]$, and $(c\bar{c})[^3S_1]$. Our calculations show that the decay widths for $\bar{B_{c}}$, $\bar{B_{c}^{*}}$, $J/ψ$ and $η_{c}$ production are 0.2251, 0.3099, 0.0537 and 0.0555 MeV, respectively, resulting in ${\cal O}(10^{4}\text{--}10^{6})$ level of $\bar{B}_c^{(*)}$ events and ${\cal O}(10^{3}\text{--}10^{5})$ level of charmonium produced at LHC per year. In particular, we find that the dominant contribution to $J/ψ$ and $η_{c}$ production via top-quark decays arises from this decay channel proposed in this work. Moreover, this multi-body top-quark decay process can serve as a sensitive probe for validating the narrow-width approximation (NWA). Finally, we provide a detailed analysis of theoretical uncertainties and differential distributions to facilitate the corresponding experimental searches. The production of a hadron associated with three quarks contains rich physical information, providing new insights for the LHC to study $B_c$ mesons and charmonia.

AI.tldr: Analysis of 1→4 decay channel for doubly heavy quarkonium production via top-quark decays within NRQCD framework, showing significant production rates for Bc/Bc* and charmonium states at LHC.
AI.motivation: To study the production of doubly heavy quarkonium (b̄c or c̄c) via top-quark decays, which provides a new channel for investigating Bc mesons and charmonia at the LHC, and to validate the narrow-width approximation through multi-body decay processes.
AI.method: Using nonrelativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework to analyze the 1→4 decay channel t → (b̄c) + c + c + s̄ and t → (c̄c) + b + c + s̄. Calculations focus on color-singlet S-wave states: (b̄c)[¹S₀], (b̄c)[³S₁], (c̄c)[¹S₀], and (c̄c)[³S₁]. Includes detailed analysis of theoretical uncertainties and differential distributions.
AI.result: Decay widths: B̄c (0.2251 MeV), B̄c* (0.3099 MeV), J/ψ (0.0537 MeV), ηc (0.0555 MeV). Production rates at LHC: O(10⁴-10⁶) Bc(*) events and O(10³-10⁵) charmonium events per year. This channel provides dominant contribution to J/ψ and ηc production via top-quark decays.
AI.conclusion: The 1→4 decay channel offers significant production rates for doubly heavy quarkonium at LHC, serves as sensitive probe for validating narrow-width approximation, and provides rich physical information for studying Bc mesons and charmonia through hadron production associated with three quarks.

title: Double-scaled bosonic and fermionic embedded ensembles, complex SYK, and the dual Hilbert space
summary: We derive the density of states along with the $2$- and $4$-point functions of embedded ensembles for both fermions and bosons in the double-scaled limit. It is shown the models are equivalent to the double-scaled Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev model, expanding the double-scaled universality class to include both fermionic and bosonic systems. The models can be solved by introducing the Wick product of non-commuting Gaussian random variables. We show that deriving the Wick product is sufficient for computing the density of states, and properties of the Wick product can be used to compute $n$-point functions directly in the energy basis. In this context, the Wick product is equivalent to normal ordering of $q$-oscillators, which leads to the duality between moments of double-scaled models and expectation values in the chord Hilbert space. By considering operator probes as a second set of oscillators, we extend the duality to compute $n$-point functions. Embedded ensembles are equivalent to complex SYK at fixed charge, and we show working directly with embedded ensembles streamlines the derivations.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that embedded ensembles for fermions and bosons in the double-scaled limit are equivalent to the double-scaled SYK model, expanding the universality class. It introduces the Wick product of non-commuting Gaussian random variables to solve these models and compute density of states and n-point functions.
AI.motivation: To extend the double-scaled universality class beyond the SYK model to include both fermionic and bosonic systems, and to develop streamlined methods for computing observables in these models using embedded ensembles.
AI.method: Introduce the Wick product of non-commuting Gaussian random variables to solve embedded ensembles. Show equivalence between Wick product and normal ordering of q-oscillators, establishing duality between moments of double-scaled models and expectation values in chord Hilbert space. Extend duality to compute n-point functions by treating operator probes as a second set of oscillators.
AI.result: Derived density of states, 2-point and 4-point functions for embedded ensembles of fermions and bosons in double-scaled limit. Showed models are equivalent to double-scaled SYK model. Demonstrated that embedded ensembles are equivalent to complex SYK at fixed charge, and that working directly with embedded ensembles simplifies derivations.
AI.conclusion: The paper expands the double-scaled universality class to include both fermionic and bosonic systems through embedded ensembles. The Wick product formalism provides an efficient method for computing observables, and the duality with q-oscillators offers a powerful framework for analyzing these models.

title: Symmetry Preserving Contact Interaction Approaches: An Overview of Meson and Diquark Form Factors
comment: 45 pages, 18 figures, review article. Accepted for publication in Particles (MDPI), 2026
summary:
We present an updated overview of the symmetry preserving Contact Interaction model in hadronic physics, developed a little over a decade ago to describe the mass spectrum and internal structure of mesons and diquarks composed of light and heavy quarks. Over the years, the Contact Interaction has evolved into a framework capable of treating both ground and excited states, providing a simple yet consistent approach to nonperturbative QCD. In this review, we examine the mass spectrum and elastic form factors of forty mesons with different spins and parities, together with their corresponding diquark partners. Importantly, we update the comparison of Contact Interaction predictions using recent results from the literature, offering a fresh perspective on the model's performance, strengths, and limitations. The analysis presented here refines previous conclusions and supports the Contact Interaction as a practical tool for hadron structure studies, with potential applications to baryons and multiquark states. We also present comparisons with other theoretical models and approaches, including lattice quantum chromodynamics, and comment on future prospects in view of ongoing and planned hadron structure experimental programs.
  In particular, forthcoming measurements at FAIR, together with future studies at Jefferson Lab and the Electron Ion Collider, are expected to provide key insights into hadron structure, with FAIR offering indirect constraints via hadron spectroscopy, hadronic interactions, and in-medium properties, while high-precision data on meson structure and form factors from Jefferson Lab and the Electron Ion Collider will provide valuable benchmarks to confront Contact Interaction based predictions.

AI.tldr: Updated review of Contact Interaction model for hadronic physics, analyzing meson/diquark mass spectra and form factors, comparing with recent results and other approaches.
AI.motivation: To provide an updated overview and assessment of the Contact Interaction model's performance in describing hadron structure, incorporating recent developments and comparisons with other theoretical approaches and experimental data.
AI.method: Contact Interaction model framework for nonperturbative QCD, analyzing 40 mesons with different spins/parities and their diquark partners, comparing predictions with recent literature results and other models including lattice QCD.
AI.result: Refined previous conclusions, supports Contact Interaction as practical tool for hadron structure studies with potential applications to baryons and multiquark states; provides comparisons with other models and experimental expectations.
AI.conclusion: Contact Interaction remains valuable framework for hadron physics; future experimental programs (FAIR, Jefferson Lab, Electron Ion Collider) will provide crucial benchmarks to test and refine model predictions.

title: Loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime: The parity-split IBP system and $\di\log$-form differential equations
summary: We develop integration-by-parts (IBP) reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals of cosmological correlators in de Sitter (dS) spacetime, demonstrating the feasibility of this approach. We identify a structural property of the dS IBP system: for an \(n\)-propagator family, it splits into \(2^n\) closed subsystems classified by the parity of the propagator indices. We further formulate a Baikov representation for loop integrals in dS space and derive the corresponding dimensional recurrence relations. In flat spacetime, intersection theory shows that \(\di\log\)-form master integrands lead to \(\di\log\)-form differential equations. Motivated by fibration intersection theory, we conjecture that this construction extends to dS integrands involving Hankel functions. We verify this conjecture in the one-loop bubble family and determine the associated alphabet.

AI.tldr: Develops IBP reduction and differential equations for massive loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime, revealing structural properties of the IBP system and extending flat-space intersection theory concepts to dS.
AI.motivation: To develop computational tools for cosmological correlators in de Sitter spacetime, particularly for massive loop integrals, which are challenging due to the curved spacetime geometry and special functions involved.
AI.method: Develops IBP reduction and differential equations for dS loop integrals; identifies structural property of dS IBP system splitting into 2^n closed subsystems by propagator index parity; formulates Baikov representation for dS loop integrals; derives dimensional recurrence relations; extends flat-space intersection theory concepts to dS using fibration intersection theory.
AI.result: Demonstrates feasibility of IBP approach for dS cosmological correlators; identifies structural property of dS IBP system; formulates Baikov representation for dS; derives dimensional recurrence relations; conjectures and verifies extension of dlog-form master integrands to dS integrands with Hankel functions in one-loop bubble family; determines associated alphabet.
AI.conclusion: The paper successfully develops IBP reduction and differential equation methods for massive loop integrals in de Sitter spacetime, revealing important structural properties and extending flat-space computational techniques to cosmological correlators, with promising implications for future calculations.

title: Dilaton-Flattened Axion Inflation
summary: We present a solvable same-sector effective theory for anomaly-inspired axion inflation, in which a heavy trace-anomaly mode dynamically backreacts on the axion potential. The tree-level elimination of the radial field resums the backreaction into a closed-form Lambert-$W$ potential, naturally flattening the hilltop potential without external plateau operators. By deriving the exact trough metric, we evaluate all the observables on the fully reduced one-field action, bypassing uncontrolled kinetic approximations. Calibrated at $N_\star=56$, reheating-compatible branches yield $r\simeq0.033$--$0.036$ and $α_s\simeq-(4.6$--$4.7)\times10^{-4}$, comfortably satisfying the current ACT/SPT/BICEP constraints. The evolution remains strictly adiabatic ($m_\perp^2/H^2\gtrsim6.1$, $Ω/H\lesssim7.6\times10^{-4}$) with negligible sound-speed and metric corrections. We provide analytic control over the constant-$w_{\rm eff}$ reheating map, the $N_{\rm re}=0$ boundary, and robustness against vacuum-offset deformations. This Lambert-$W$ backbone establishes a precise, deformable benchmark for confining axion inflation, with microscopic matching and reheating microphysics accessible as systematic EFT refinements.

AI.tldr: Anomaly-inspired axion inflation model with heavy trace-anomaly mode backreaction resummed into Lambert-W potential, yielding precise predictions consistent with current CMB constraints.
AI.motivation: To develop a solvable effective theory for anomaly-inspired axion inflation that properly accounts for heavy trace-anomaly mode backreaction, avoiding uncontrolled kinetic approximations and providing analytic control over inflationary observables.
AI.method: Tree-level elimination of radial field resums backreaction into closed-form Lambert-W potential; derivation of exact trough metric; evaluation of observables on fully reduced one-field action; analytic treatment of reheating map and robustness analysis.
AI.result: For N⋆=56, reheating-compatible branches yield tensor-to-scalar ratio r≈0.033-0.036 and running αs≈-(4.6-4.7)×10⁻⁴, satisfying ACT/SPT/BICEP constraints; strictly adiabatic evolution with negligible sound-speed and metric corrections.
AI.conclusion: The Lambert-W potential establishes a precise, deformable benchmark for confining axion inflation with analytic control, providing a foundation for systematic EFT refinements including microscopic matching and reheating microphysics.

title: The OPE Approach to Renormalization: Operator Mixing
summary: We extend the OPE-based renormalization algorithm to composite operators with operator mixing, focusing on scalar operators in $φ^4$ and $φ^3$ models. Using the OPE of operators with a fundamental field, we show that the $Z$-factors of these composite operators are determined by OPE coefficients of lower-dimensional traceless symmetric tensor operators, and establish a recursive renormalization framework. We report the five-loop anomalous dimensions for operators with $Δ\le5$ in the $φ^4$ model and the two-loop anomalous dimensions for operators with $Δ\le10$ in the $φ^3$ model. These results further demonstrate the versatility and efficiency of the OPE-based algorithm.

AI.tldr: OPE-based renormalization algorithm extended to composite operators with operator mixing, applied to scalar operators in φ⁴ and φ³ models, yielding multi-loop anomalous dimensions.
AI.motivation: To extend the OPE-based renormalization algorithm to handle composite operators with operator mixing, which is important for understanding renormalization of interacting quantum field theories beyond simple cases.
AI.method: Using the OPE of operators with a fundamental field, showing that Z-factors of composite operators are determined by OPE coefficients of lower-dimensional traceless symmetric tensor operators, establishing a recursive renormalization framework.
AI.result: Five-loop anomalous dimensions for operators with Δ≤5 in the φ⁴ model and two-loop anomalous dimensions for operators with Δ≤10 in the φ³ model.
AI.conclusion: The results demonstrate the versatility and efficiency of the OPE-based algorithm for renormalization of composite operators with operator mixing.

title: Echoes of Global Cosmic Strings
summary: If the Universe underwent a cosmic phase transition, it may have left behind a network of cosmic strings. When these strings arise from the breaking of a gauge symmetry, their decay produces a significant stochastic background of gravitational waves. In contrast, if they originate from the breaking of a global symmetry, their decay predominantly yields Nambu-Goldstone bosons, which can persist as dark matter or dark radiation. In this work, we assess the detectability of this particle spectrum using a range of cosmological probes. We employ semi-numerical methods to estimate the resulting energy density and compute the associated matter power spectrum. We then compare these predictions with observations of the cosmic microwave background, Lyman-$α$ forest, large-scale structure surveys, and the UV luminosity function, thereby deriving constraints on the Nambu-Goldstone boson mass and the symmetry-breaking scale. Finally, we present projections for the sensitivity of upcoming cosmic microwave background missions.

AI.tldr: Analysis of detectability of Nambu-Goldstone bosons from cosmic string decay using cosmological probes to constrain particle mass and symmetry-breaking scale.
AI.motivation: Cosmic strings from phase transitions produce different decay products depending on symmetry type: gauge symmetry yields gravitational waves, while global symmetry yields Nambu-Goldstone bosons that could be dark matter/dark radiation. Need to assess detectability of these particles.
AI.method: Use semi-numerical methods to estimate energy density from cosmic string decay, compute associated matter power spectrum, and compare predictions with multiple cosmological observations (CMB, Lyman-α forest, large-scale structure surveys, UV luminosity function).
AI.result: Derive constraints on Nambu-Goldstone boson mass and symmetry-breaking scale from observational comparisons, and present sensitivity projections for upcoming CMB missions.
AI.conclusion: Cosmological probes can effectively constrain properties of Nambu-Goldstone bosons from cosmic string decay, with upcoming CMB missions offering improved sensitivity for detection.

title: Decrease of the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation induced by backreaction in the Bose-Einstein condensate
summary: We analytically study the effect of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation on its entanglement entropy in the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC). The backreaction is expected to play an essential role in the decrease of the entanglement entropy and in realizing the Page curve. Since the BEC theory has microscopic Hamiltonian and thus exhibits unitarity, it is desirable to reproduce the Page curve explicitly by using the Hamiltonian. In order to analyze this in a concrete example, we study the BEC with a step-like configuration that has been extensively studied in the literature. By using the microscopic theory, we derive an explicit form of backreaction from analog Hawking radiation. Combining it with the known results of the Bogoliubov coefficients, we analytically compute the entanglement entropy of the Hawking radiation, and show that it decreases as expected due to the backreaction for sufficiently low energy modes over a wide range of the parameter characterizing the step-like configuration.

AI.tldr: Analytical study of backreaction effects from analog Hawking radiation on entanglement entropy in BEC systems, showing entanglement entropy decreases due to backreaction for low-energy modes across wide parameter ranges.
