AI.motivation: To understand how backreaction from analog Hawking radiation affects entanglement entropy and contributes to realizing the Page curve in unitary BEC systems with microscopic Hamiltonians.
AI.method: Using microscopic theory of BEC with step-like configuration to derive explicit backreaction form from analog Hawking radiation, combining with known Bogoliubov coefficients to analytically compute entanglement entropy.
AI.result: Entanglement entropy of Hawking radiation decreases as expected due to backreaction for sufficiently low energy modes over a wide range of the step-like configuration parameter.
AI.conclusion: Backreaction plays essential role in decreasing entanglement entropy and realizing Page curve in unitary BEC systems, providing explicit analytical demonstration of these effects.

title: The ODE/IM Correspondence between $C (2)^{(2)}$-type Linear Problems and 2d $\mathcal{N} = 1$ SCFT
summary: We study the ODE/IM correspondence between the linear problem associated with the supersymmetric affine Toda field equation for the twisted affine Lie superalgebra $C (2)^{(2)} = \mathfrak{osp} (2 | 2)^{(2)}$ and two-dimensional $\mathcal{N} = 1$ superconformal field theories (SCFTs). On the ODE side, we introduce a boundary condition more suitable for the conformal limit and the subsequent WKB analysis and diagonalize the resulting Lax operator. This leads to a WKB expansion from which we extract the WKB periods and non-local conserved quantities up to tenth order. On the IM side, we compute the eigenvalues of the local integrals of motion on the cylinder in both the Neveu-Schwarz and Ramond sectors of 2d $\mathcal{N} = 1$ SCFTs. We then compare the two sides and verify, up to sixth order, that the WKB periods coincide with the eigenvalues of the local integrals of motion for highest-weight states in the Neveu-Schwarz sector.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes an ODE/IM correspondence between the supersymmetric affine Toda field equation for twisted affine Lie superalgebra C(2)^(2) and 2D N=1 superconformal field theories, verifying matching of WKB periods with local IM eigenvalues up to sixth order.
AI.motivation: To extend the ODE/IM correspondence framework to supersymmetric cases, specifically connecting the linear problem of supersymmetric affine Toda field equations for twisted affine Lie superalgebras with two-dimensional N=1 superconformal field theories.
AI.method: On ODE side: introduced suitable boundary conditions for conformal limit, diagonalized Lax operator, performed WKB analysis to extract WKB periods and non-local conserved quantities up to tenth order. On IM side: computed eigenvalues of local integrals of motion on cylinder in both Neveu-Schwarz and Ramond sectors of 2D N=1 SCFTs.
AI.result: Successfully verified up to sixth order that WKB periods from ODE side coincide with eigenvalues of local integrals of motion for highest-weight states in the Neveu-Schwarz sector of 2D N=1 SCFTs.
AI.conclusion: The paper establishes a concrete ODE/IM correspondence for supersymmetric affine Toda field theory associated with C(2)^(2) = osp(2|2)^(2), demonstrating matching between WKB periods and local IM eigenvalues in the Neveu-Schwarz sector, extending the correspondence framework to supersymmetric cases.

title: Correlators in $T\bar{T}$ and Root-$T\bar{T}$ Deformed CFTs
summary: Quasi-primary correlators in two-dimensional conformal field theories deformed simultaneously by $T\bar T$ and root-$T\bar T$ are studied. A path-integral formulation motivated by the geometric realization of the combined deformation is used to develop a geometric framework for evaluating the deformed correlators. Within this framework, the two-point function is obtained to all orders in the $T\bar T$ coupling and to leading order in the root-$T\bar T$ coupling, while the leading correction to the three-point function is computed. It is further shown that the deformed two-point correlator admits a kernel representation as a weighted average of undeformed CFT correlators over conformal dimensions. This representation is derived explicitly for both the pure $T\bar T$ deformation and the combined flow. In this way, the mixed $T\bar T$/root-$T\bar T$ deformation is incorporated into the geometric description of irrelevant deformations, and the structure of local correlators beyond the pure $T\bar T$ case is characterized more explicitly.

AI.tldr: Study of quasi-primary correlators in 2D CFTs deformed by both T\bar T and root-T\bar T operators using geometric path-integral formulation, deriving two-point functions to all orders in T\bar T and leading order in root-T\bar T, with kernel representation as weighted average over conformal dimensions.
AI.motivation: To extend the geometric description of irrelevant deformations beyond pure T\bar T case by incorporating mixed T\bar T/root-T\bar T deformations, and to characterize the structure of local correlators in these combined deformations more explicitly.
AI.method: Path-integral formulation motivated by geometric realization of combined deformation, developing geometric framework for evaluating deformed correlators. Uses kernel representation as weighted average of undeformed CFT correlators over conformal dimensions.
AI.result: Obtained two-point function to all orders in T\bar T coupling and leading order in root-T\bar T coupling; computed leading correction to three-point function; derived explicit kernel representation for both pure T\bar T deformation and combined flow.
AI.conclusion: Successfully incorporated mixed T\bar T/root-T\bar T deformation into geometric description of irrelevant deformations, providing more explicit characterization of local correlator structure beyond pure T\bar T case.

title: Boundary lines and Askey-Wilson type moments
summary: The Wilson line defect half-indices for 3d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theories with boundary confining phases admit a formulation in terms of the Askey-Wilson type moments. In the dual Landau-Ginzburg description the dual line operators can be realized as vortex line defects which induce singular behavior of chiral multiplets associated with the minimal monopole operators, together with additional one-dimensional degrees of freedom. By incorporating such a singular structure as an effective spin shift into the index computation, we obtain exact closed-form expressions for the line defect half-indices which are Askey-Wilson type moments.

AI.tldr: Wilson line defect half-indices for 3D N=2 gauge theories with boundary confining phases are expressed as Askey-Wilson type moments, with dual vortex line defects realized through singular chiral multiplet behavior and effective spin shifts.
AI.motivation: To establish a precise mathematical formulation for Wilson line defect half-indices in 3D N=2 gauge theories with boundary confining phases, connecting them to known mathematical structures (Askey-Wilson moments) and providing a dual Landau-Ginzburg description.
AI.method: 1. Formulate Wilson line defect half-indices in terms of Askey-Wilson type moments. 2. Develop dual Landau-Ginzburg description where dual line operators are realized as vortex line defects inducing singular behavior of chiral multiplets associated with minimal monopole operators. 3. Incorporate singular structure as effective spin shift into index computation to obtain exact closed-form expressions.
AI.result: Obtained exact closed-form expressions for line defect half-indices that are Askey-Wilson type moments, establishing a precise mathematical correspondence between gauge theory observables and orthogonal polynomial moments.
AI.conclusion: Wilson line defect half-indices in 3D N=2 gauge theories with boundary confining phases can be systematically computed as Askey-Wilson type moments through a dual description involving vortex line defects and effective spin shifts, providing exact mathematical expressions for these observables.

title: Monodromy Defects for Electric-Magnetic Duality, Hyperbolic Space, and Lines
summary: In this note we explore monodromy defects for non-invertible symmetries in Maxwell theory, exploiting the conformal mapping to $AdS_{3} \times S^{1}$. With this approach we recover the spectrum of the defect conformal primaries. We also dedicate some time discussing the behaviour of Wilson/'t Hooft lines in the presence of such a monodromy defect, and highlight the following aspects of their behaviour: i) the lines can terminate on the defect, ii) lines of the unit electric (magnetic) charge may seize to be indecomposable, and can be represented as integer powers of some more elementary lines, and iii) they behave as topological objects when brought close to the defect, and this behaviour is governed by a Chern-Simons theory.

AI.tldr: Study of monodromy defects for non-invertible symmetries in Maxwell theory using AdS₃×S¹ mapping, analyzing defect primaries and Wilson/'t Hooft line behavior near defects.
AI.motivation: To understand monodromy defects in Maxwell theory with non-invertible symmetries, particularly how Wilson and 't Hooft lines interact with such defects, using conformal mapping techniques to simplify analysis.
AI.method: Employ conformal mapping to AdS₃×S¹ geometry to analyze monodromy defects, study defect conformal primaries spectrum, and examine Wilson/'t Hooft line behavior including termination, decomposition properties, and topological aspects near defects.
AI.result: Recovered spectrum of defect conformal primaries; identified three key behaviors: 1) Wilson/'t Hooft lines can terminate on defects, 2) unit charge lines become decomposable into powers of more elementary lines, 3) lines behave topologically near defects with Chern-Simons theory governing this behavior.
AI.conclusion: Monodromy defects in Maxwell theory with non-invertible symmetries exhibit rich structure where Wilson/'t Hooft lines show termination, decomposition, and topological behavior near defects, with Chern-Simons theory emerging as governing framework for line-defect interactions.

title: Extraordinary Surface Criticalities for Interacting Fermions
summary: Interacting fermions exhibit a rich landscape of surface defects and associated critical phenomena. We investigate novel surface critical behavior in the three-dimensional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model. For a class of defect renormalization group flows, we obtain exact infrared solutions and show how fermionic anomalies are encoded in the resulting surface dynamics. We further uncover emergent topological and geometric structures in the defect coupling space, and comment on their relation to a defect analogue of the CFT distance conjecture.

AI.tldr: Exact solutions for surface critical behavior in 3D Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model reveal fermionic anomaly encoding, emergent topological/geometric structures in defect coupling space, and connections to defect CFT distance conjecture.
AI.motivation: To investigate novel surface critical behavior in interacting fermion systems, particularly exploring how fermionic anomalies manifest in surface dynamics and uncovering emergent structures in defect coupling space.
AI.method: Study defect renormalization group flows in the three-dimensional Gross-Neveu-Yukawa model, obtaining exact infrared solutions through analytical methods.
AI.result: Exact infrared solutions demonstrate how fermionic anomalies are encoded in surface dynamics, revealing emergent topological and geometric structures in defect coupling space.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes connections between defect critical phenomena, fermionic anomalies, and emergent geometric structures, suggesting a defect analogue of the CFT distance conjecture.

title: Sampling the Graviton Pole and Deprojecting the Swampland
summary: We develop a primal bootstrap framework for effective field theories in the presence of a graviton pole, based on finite-resolution sampling rather than smearing, while also allowing direct control over the number of subtractions. We show that this approach reproduces the known projective bounds obtained from smearing in $D{\ge}6$, while yielding slightly stronger bounds in $D{=}5$. This method also makes it straightforward to impose linearized unitarity directly and provides an access to the extremal spectra. Applying the method to crossing-symmetric dispersion relations, we derive new non-projective bounds that fix the overall scale of the EFT couplings. In $D{=}5$, for example, we find that $\frac{M}{M_{\rm P}}{\lesssim}7.8$, showing that the EFT cutoff cannot be taken parametrically larger than the Planck scale. At the extremal values of the couplings, the spectra exhibit a surprising structure: for projective bounds, they exhibit peaks around quadratic Regge-like trajectories, while for the non-projective bounds they form sharp quadratic bands. In the latter case, the leading coefficients further display an inverse-quadratic dependence on the band number.

AI.tldr: A primal bootstrap framework for gravitational EFTs using finite-resolution sampling instead of smearing, yielding stronger bounds in D=5 and enabling direct linearized unitarity constraints and extremal spectrum analysis.
AI.motivation: To develop a more direct bootstrap approach for gravitational effective field theories that avoids smearing techniques, allows control over subtraction numbers, and provides better access to extremal spectra and unitarity constraints.
AI.method: Primal bootstrap framework based on finite-resolution sampling rather than smearing, applied to crossing-symmetric dispersion relations with direct linearized unitarity imposition.
AI.result: Reproduces known projective bounds in D≥6, yields stronger bounds in D=5, derives new non-projective bounds fixing EFT coupling scales, and reveals extremal spectra with quadratic Regge-like trajectories or sharp quadratic bands.
AI.conclusion: The finite-resolution sampling approach provides a more direct bootstrap method for gravitational EFTs, revealing that EFT cutoffs cannot be parametrically larger than Planck scale and uncovering structured extremal spectra with quadratic patterns.

title: Kontorovich-Lebedev-Fourier Space for de Sitter Correlators
summary: In this work, we build a novel frequency-momentum space for $(d+1)$-dimensional de Sitter (dS) correlators from first principles. This construction follows directly from the decomposition into unitary irreducible representations (UIRs) of the spacetime isometry group $\mathrm{SO}(1,d+1)$. While the spatial momentum space is given by the standard $d$-dimensional Fourier transform, the frequency space arises from diagonalising the quadratic Casimir operator, leading to the $(d+1)$-dimensional Kontorovich-Lebedev-Fourier (KLF) transform. We show that square-integrable functions decompose only along the principal series, whereas more general functions can receive discrete contributions from other UIRs. Applying this framework to the bulk CFT two-point function reproduces its Källén-Lehmann representation. Using the path integral formulation, we derive the Feynman rules for in-in perturbation theory in KLF space, leading to the introduction of KLF-space correlators, which are simply related to late-time correlation functions through a reduction formula. Furthermore, the KLF-space formulation sheds light on the simple mathematical structure of perturbative computations. In particular, the propagators take the form of simple rational functions, and tree-level diagrams can be written as spectral integrals over known meromorphic functions, as demonstrated in the example of the single-exchange four-point function. At the loop level, we show, through the example of the self-energy correction to the scalar propagator, that the group-theoretical nature of the construction allows the momentum integral to be recast as an orthogonality relation among $\mathrm{SO}(1,d+1)$ Clebsch-Gordan coefficients.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs a frequency-momentum space for (d+1)-dimensional de Sitter correlators using group theory, introducing the Kontorovich-Lebedev-Fourier transform and deriving Feynman rules for perturbation theory.
AI.motivation: To develop a first-principles framework for de Sitter correlators that reveals their underlying mathematical structure through group-theoretical decomposition, enabling simpler perturbative computations.
AI.method: Constructs frequency-momentum space by decomposing into unitary irreducible representations of SO(1,d+1), using Kontorovich-Lebedev-Fourier transform for frequency space and standard Fourier transform for momentum space. Derives Feynman rules for in-in perturbation theory in this space.
AI.result: Shows that propagators become simple rational functions in KLF space, tree-level diagrams reduce to spectral integrals over meromorphic functions, and loop integrals can be recast as orthogonality relations among Clebsch-Gordan coefficients. Reproduces Källén-Lehmann representation for bulk CFT two-point function.
AI.conclusion: The KLF-space formulation provides a powerful group-theoretical framework that simplifies perturbative computations in de Sitter space, revealing the underlying mathematical structure and enabling systematic calculations of correlation functions.
